applicability: Choosing between placing more scopes and enlarging a ring.
Confirming that a `RunConfig` ring override actually reached the runtime.
directions: Add `--enable-scope-stats` to the entry and pass `RunConfig(enable_scope_stats=True, save_kernels=True)`.
Read line 1 to confirm the effective capacities before interpreting any peak.

Pair begin/end records per ring and per site; use `scope_high_water`, `real_occupancy`, and `scope_alloc` to choose between scope placement, shrinking intermediates, splitting a scope, and ring sizing.
Use `python -m simpler_setup.tools.scope_stats_plot` rather than a runtime-relative script path that may not exist in a checkout.
effects: Scope stats reveal per-site peaks and effective capacities, but require an actual run and add DFX records.
Enlarging a ring is immediate but treats the symptom; splitting a scope or shrinking intermediates reduces the peak structurally.
High-frequency scope samples attribute pressure precisely but can perturb the schedule and produce dropped records.
invariants: `--compile-only` never reaches the runtime and records no scope stats.
Collector drops make reported peaks lower bounds; re-run with less concurrency before trusting them.
Reclaim happens only when the allocator has to wait, so an oversized ring may never reclaim and a scoped program can report the same frontier as an unscoped one.
Oversizing task window, dependency pool, or heap increases the static arena and can fail before kernel launch.
principle: `scope_stats` writes one sample at every scope boundary: task-window, heap, dependency-pool head/tail, and tensormap usage. It works on both L2 and L3 paths; L2 writes under `dfx_outputs/scope_stats/`, L3 per rank and dispatch under `dfx_outputs/rank<N>/d<K>/scope_stats/`. Line 1 is run metadata carrying schema version, `fatal`, `dropped`, and the effective capacities `task_window_max`, `heap_max`, and `dep_pool_max` as arrays indexed by ring, plus `tensormap_max`. Every later line is a `begin` or `end` sample with a source `site`, depth, ring, and head/tail counters. In schema version 6 heap counters are monotonic cumulative bytes. Pair a begin with its end to compute `scope_high_water = end.head - begin.tail`, an upper bound on pressure reached; `real_occupancy = end.head - end.tail`, what is still held at exit; and `scope_alloc = end.head - begin.head`, allocation throughput independent of reclaim. A ring near capacity while others are near zero indicates auto-scope collapse or all work at one depth. High high-water with low live occupancy means the scope streams and reclaim keeps up. High live occupancy at exit means a long-lived allocation is pinned in that ring. Only begin records at the file tail indicate the run wedged inside that scope; the last open site is where the ring filled. `dropped > 0` means collector back-pressure and makes peaks lower bounds. `fatal: true` means a fatal was latched and later records are diagnostic only. `enable_scope_stats` requires an actual execution; `--compile-only` records nothing. Any DFX flag forces `save_kernels=True` so the work directory survives. Render with `python -m simpler_setup.tools.scope_stats_plot <scope_stats.jsonl>` or pair records directly. Deadlock codes are reported through a generic host ACL error; the real cause is the `orch_error_code` line: 1 `SCOPE_DEADLOCK`, 2 `HEAP_RING_DEADLOCK`, 3 `FLOW_CONTROL_DEADLOCK` often from nesting on the same ring, 4 `DEP_POOL_OVERFLOW`, and 11 `TENSORMAP_OVERFLOW`. Oversizing all rings can instead fail with `rtMalloc 207001` before execution.
questions: The local runtime's effective ring capacities and whether `_apply_ring_overrides` is reached on both L2 and L3 dispatch paths were not exercised.
risks: Treating the metadata line as a scope sample and pairing it with a begin record.
Assuming a peak is exact when `dropped > 0`.
Reading only the generic `507018 ACL_ERROR_RT_AICPU_EXCEPTION` and missing the `orch_error_code` that identifies the ring resource.
Using a runtime/tools path that is absent from a pypto-lib checkout instead of the `simpler_setup.tools` module form.
summary: `enable_scope_stats` records task-window, heap, dependency-pool, and tensormap usage at every scope boundary. The first JSONL line proves effective ring capacities; paired begin/end samples show high-water, live occupancy, and allocation throughput, while `orch_error_code` names the resource that wedged.
title: Scope Stats and Ring Deadlock Diagnosis
